nodes.description: Serializer layer separates API response format from internal model representation

inputs.prompt: Evaluate serializer layer. Check: (1) dedicated serializer classes for API responses, (2) serializers define which fields to expose, (3) nested serializers for associations, (4) conditional field inclusion based on user role/permissions, (5) controllers use serializers rather than rendering models directly.
inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate serializer pattern: 1) Are API responses shaped through serializer classes? 2) Do serializers control field exposure per role? 3) Is serialization separate from models? 4) Are nested relationships efficient? Score 0-4.

nodes.description: Background jobs properly used for async operations (email, indexing, cleanup)

inputs.prompt: Evaluate background job architecture. Check: (1) Sidekiq or similar job framework configured, (2) separate job classes for different async operations, (3) scheduled jobs for periodic tasks (cleanup, stats, etc.), (4) proper error handling and retry logic in jobs, (5) email sending delegated to background jobs.
inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate background job architecture: 1) Are long tasks offloaded to background jobs? 2) Is job queue properly configured? 3) Are jobs idempotent and retryable? 4) Are scheduled jobs defined for maintenance? Score 0-6.

nodes.description: Plugin architecture supports extension points for customization

inputs.prompt: Evaluate plugin/extension architecture. Check: (1) plugin loading mechanism, (2) extension points or hooks for plugins to register callbacks, (3) plugin API for adding routes, controllers, models, (4) plugin isolation (plugins don't break core), (5) event system or middleware pattern for extensibility.
inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate plugin architecture: 1) Is there a plugin registration mechanism? 2) Can plugins hook into core events? 3) Are plugin APIs well-defined? 4) Is plugin isolation maintained? Score 0-5.

nodes.description: Trust level system is cleanly encapsulated with promotion logic separated

inputs.prompt: Evaluate trust level system design. Check: (1) trust level constants/enum cleanly defined, (2) promotion logic encapsulated in dedicated class, (3) TL3 requirements model with configurable thresholds, (4) trust level gates integrated with permissions system, (5) clean separation of TL calculation from TL enforcement.
inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate trust level design: 1) Is trust level logic centralized? 2) Are promotion rules configurable? 3) Is trust level checked consistently? 4) Are thresholds data-driven? Score 0-5.

nodes.description: Real-time messaging uses proper pub/sub pattern (MessageBus or similar)

inputs.prompt: Evaluate real-time messaging design. Check: (1) pub/sub messaging infrastructure (MessageBus, ActionCable, or custom), (2) channels defined for different event types (topic updates, notifications, user status), (3) proper message publishing from models/services, (4) client-side subscription mechanism, (5) message bus backed by Redis or similar for scalability.
inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate real-time messaging: 1) Is there a pub/sub system for real-time updates? 2) Are channels scoped per user/topic? 3) Is auth enforced on channels? 4) Is the system scalable? Score 0-5.

nodes.description: Search system properly uses PostgreSQL tsvector/tsquery for full-text search

inputs.prompt: Evaluate search system design. Check: (1) PostgreSQL tsvector columns for full-text search, (2) GIN indexes on tsvector columns, (3) search query builder with filter support, (4) search ranking/weighting logic, (5) multi-language ts_config support, (6) search index update triggers or callbacks.
inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate search architecture: 1) Is full-text search using proper features (tsvector/GIN)? 2) Are indexes maintained efficiently? 3) Is ranking tuned? 4) Are results paginated and cached? Score 0-5.

nodes.description: Overall code quality - naming conventions, structure, documentation

inputs.prompt: Evaluate overall code quality. Check: (1) consistent naming conventions (Ruby style snake_case), (2) logical file organization, (3) appropriate use of Ruby/Rails idioms, (4) meaningful variable and method names, (5) code comments where needed for complex logic, (6) DRY principles followed, (7) proper error handling patterns.
inputs.rubric_prompt: Evaluate code quality: 1) Is codebase well-organized with consistent structure? 2) Are naming conventions consistent? 3) Is there proper error handling? 4) Are DB queries optimized? 5) Is test infrastructure present? Score 0-10.
